title: Nanopublication extraction schema (reading14)
description: Schema for decomposing paper conclusions into individually falsifiable assertions, binding each assertion to a minimal sufficient evidence fragment with a pointable source location, and recording the full assertion->evidence->paper->author->year->version provenance chain. result.json is the export artifact; it must be valid UTF-8 JSON parseable without manual cleanup. Additional fields required by the case output_contract are allowed (additionalProperties=true) and must be merged in alongside these fields. Relation is a recommended closed vocabulary: out-of-vocabulary verbs are WARNINGS in src/nanopub.py (they require an explicit note), never silent hard failures.

schema_version.description: Version of this schema; bump when field semantics change.

status_detail.description: Human-readable reason when status is partial or failed.

generated_at.description: ISO-8601 UTC timestamp of this export, e.g. 2026-11-23T12:00:00Z.

assertions.description: One entry per single claim. Never put a whole paragraph in one assertion.text.

unreported.description: Things the paper does not report; never guessed, never written as facts.

conflicts.description: Assertion<->evidence or within-source conflicts; both sides kept, no silent deletion.

status.description: success=all required assertions extracted and validated; partial=some sources/assertions unusable but a usable subset exported; failed=no usable text/assertion.

source_kind.description: The kind of thing the evidence points into.

version.description: Version of the source: published, author-accepted, preprint-v1, v1, v2, ... Use 'unknown' when the version cannot be determined.

source_id.description: Unique short id inside this result, e.g. 'src-1' or a stable DOI prefix.

authors.description: Author names; preferred form 'FamilyName, GivenName'. Empty is an error: provenance needs at least one author.

year.description: Publication year; null only when genuinely unknown and then noted in note.

identifiers.description: At least one identifier required; DOI preferred. 'unknown' when none can be found (then note must say why).

content_hash.description: Optional sha256 of the exact text file the quotes were taken from; enables repeatability.

entity_type.description: Coarse type of the assertion endpoints. 'other' allowed but note should give a finer label.

label.description: Surface form as used in the assertion, e.g. 'BRCA1', 'tumor growth'.

normalized.description: Canonical/normalized form (uniprot gene symbol, MeSH term, etc.) when available; otherwise repeat the label.

relation_type.description: Class of the relation. causal=one thing changes another (sign captured by relation verb + direction); associative=co-occurring/predictive but no causal claim; comparative=greater/less/equal/different; definitional=is-a/part-of/expresses/encodes/binds; quantitative=measured value; methodological=evaluated/detected/treated by.

relation.description: Lowercase snake_case predicate verb from the recommended vocabulary (see $defs/relation_vocab list). Out-of-vocabulary verbs are a WARNING in src/nanopub.py and require a decomposition.note explaining the mapping.

polarity.description: affirmative = the relation holds; negated = the paper says the relation does NOT hold (e.g. 'X did not increase Y').

direction.description: Sign of the effect. positive for increases/promotes/greater_than; negative for decreases/inhibits/less_than; neutral for associative/definitional/quantitative/methodological.

quantifier.description: How generally the claim is stated. Use 'specific' for a particular dose/sample/cohort; 'not_stated' when the paper does not quantify.

condition_slot.description: The qualifier slot the condition fills; keeps scope/qualifiers attached to the assertion instead of dropping them.

verbatim.description: The original qualifier phrase when the value is a paraphrase.

certainty_level.description: reported = stated as a finding; inferred = read off data/figures or composed from multiple statements; speculative = hedged (may/might/suggests).

basis.description: Why this level was chosen, e.g. the verbatim sentence or the figure read-off.

decomposition_method.description: direct=one clause already; coordination_split=split a compound subject/object/predicate; causal_split=split a chained cause->effect; condition_extraction=lifted qualifiers into conditions.

note.description: What was split and why; required whenever method is not 'direct' or relation is out-of-vocabulary.

quote_type.description: verbatim=exact text from the source; paraphrase=restated (must be flagged, weaker); figure_description/table_description/equation=structured description when the evidence is not running text.

relation_to_assertion.description: direct=quote states the relation; inferred=quote gives data/stats from which the assertion is read off (must give sufficiency.reason); context=quote only gives background, NOT support.

sufficiency_judgment.description: sufficient=quote alone supports the assertion; partial=quote supports part of it (conditions/comparator missing); insufficient=quote does not support the assertion.

page.description: PDF page number when the source has pages; null when not applicable (e.g. JATS-only input).

paragraph.description: 1-based paragraph index within the section or document.

figure.description: e.g. 'Fig. 2B'. Use when evidence is a figure; then quote_type must be figure_description.

pointer.description: Free-text, unambiguous human pointer, e.g. 'p.3, Results, para 2, sent 1' or 'Fig. 2B, right panel'.

start.description: 0-based char offset of the quote in the extracted text file.

text_file.description: Path/name of the text file the offsets refer to.

evidence_id.description: Unique id, e.g. 'e1'. Referenced by provenance.evidence_id.

quote.description: Minimal sufficient fragment: the shortest verbatim span that still supports the relation. Not the whole paragraph; must be grep-able in the extracted text when quote_type=verbatim.

reason.description: Why the quote is/ is not sufficient; REQUIRED when judgment != sufficient or relation_to_assertion != direct.

minimality_note.description: How the quote was minimized, e.g. 'trimmed to the clause carrying subject+verb+object'.

chain.description: Exactly [assertion_id, evidence_id, source_id] in that order; verified by src/nanopub.py.

assertion_status.description: supported=has sufficient binding; unsupported=no supporting fragment found (kept, not fabricated); conflict=assertion and evidence disagree (kept side by side); not_extractable=cannot be decomposed/read (e.g. no text layer, figure-only).

text.description: Normalized single claim, conditions kept in-line or in conditions[]. One subject, one relation, one object; no compound coordination, no causal chaining.

source_text.description: The verbatim original sentence(s) this assertion was decomposed from; used for the conditions-preserved and coordination checks.

question.description: Which of the four challenge questions the check serves.

issue_type.description: The five rubric-named quality problems plus 'other'.

note.description: Both sides kept; describe the disagreement, do not pick one silently.
